site_assessment.who_runs_it: waqf.zfiusa.org is a subdomain run by Zakat Foundation of India USA (ZFI USA / zfiusa.org), a US-based nonprofit that fundraises for charitable/religious causes in India (per its own homepage: 'Zakat Foundation of India USA'). No specific author, dev team, 'About', or contact info is present on the waqf subdomain itself identifying who built or maintains this particular tool.
site_assessment.credibility_notes: This is NOT an original/independent survey of Waqf properties. The per-property 'Report Card' pages (e.g. /properties-details/36/TSHY0091-DH001) are structurally and textually identical to the official Government of India Waqf Management System of India (WAMSI, wamsi.nic.in, Ministry of Minority Affairs) property report cards -- same field labels (Waqf Classification, Waqif Name, Gazette Notification Details, Property Current Status, litigation/court-case sub-tables), and the scraped page even carries a WAMSI-style 'Report Card As on October 30, 2024' timestamp. ZFI USA's site is best understood as an unofficial third-party mirror/frontend that ingested a snapshot of WAMSI's public Waqf property records and put a searchable UI in front of them. The claimed count of 45,191 Telangana properties is real and independently verified via the site's own API (recordsTotal=45191), and it plausibly reflects genuine WAMSI data (including real-looking litigation/encroachment case details -- petitioner names, court case numbers, hearing dates), which is valuable for the hackathon. However: (1) it is a secondary/unofficial mirror, not an authoritative source in itself -- cite it as 'via ZFI USA mirror of WAMSI data' rather than as an independent finding; (2) the data snapshot is dated (Oct 30, 2024 per the report-card timestamp), so may be stale versus current WAMSI records; (3) the site's hosting is fragile -- it became unreachable (connection resets/timeouts) partway through this scrape after a modest burst of API/page requests, which is a reliability concern for a live demo relying on it; (4) no way to verify ZFI USA had authorization to mirror this data, or that the mirror is complete/unmodified versus the source.

notes: Site structure: the homepage (https://waqf.zfiusa.org) has a state/district/sub-district dropdown search form backed by real JSON endpoints: GET /waqf-districts?state_id=ID, GET /waqf-subdistricts?district_id=ID, and a DataTables server-side endpoint GET /state-properties?state_id=ID&district_id=ID&sub_district_id=ID&start=N&length=N&draw=N which returns {draw, recordsTotal, recordsFiltered, data:[...]}. For Telangana (state_id=36) recordsTotal=45191, confirmed by direct API call -- this independently verifies the site's claimed 45,191-property figure. Unusually, the endpoint enforced no page-size cap during this session -- a single request with length=46000 returned ALL 45,191 Telangana records in one ~10s response. That FULL raw pull (waqf_id, property_id, internal numeric district/subDistrict/village codes, and a numeric propertyType code per record -- no resolved name/address/area/status) is saved separately at ~/waqftrace/data/raw/zfiusa_waqf_bulk_index_full_45191.json (10.8MB, all 45,191 rows) since embedding it in full here would have produced an impractically large (26MB) deliverable. This main file instead includes a stratified random sample (150 per district x 10 districts = 1500 records, seed=42, reproducible) of that bulk index to demonstrate coverage across every Telangana district, plus one FULLY detail-scraped record (first entry in `properties`) showing the rich field set genuinely available per-property. Resolved name/address/area/status/locality/litigation data only exists on the individual detail page at /properties-details/{state_id}/{waqf_id}-{property_id}, an ~860KB HTML 'Report Card' page per property matching WAMSI's official report-card format (address, land type, area, boundaries, survey details, estimated value, current status, and full litigation/court-case sub-records where applicable). The one scraped example, TSHY0091-DH001, is a Dargah/graveyard in Amberpet, Hyderabad, currently in High Court litigation over encroachment -- directly relevant to WaqfTrace's anti-encroachment angle. District-level breakdown of all 45,191 records (from the full bulk pull): {"Hyderabad": 3714, "Adilabad": 3079, "Karimnagar": 2685, "Khammam": 1321, "Unknown": 4, "Mahbubnagar": 6315, "Medak": 8429, "Nalgonda": 4144, "Nizamabad": 5727, "Rangareddy": 7013, "Warangal": 2760}. Raw propertyType code frequency across all 45,191 records (meaning NOT decoded -- only one example was resolved: code '5' = 'Dargah or Mazaar or Makbara' for the one scraped record; do not assume this mapping holds for other codes without further verification): {"5": 2180, "3": 36, "7": 9169, "2": 10572, "15": 3058, "4": 7306, "19": 404, "22": 2751, "18": 1391, "8": 1048, "10": 1141, "13": 63, "12": 42, "23": 124, "16": 62, "21": 18, "9": 8, "6": 12, "14": 9, "1": 5787, "": 4, "20": 1, "17": 4, "11": 1}. Scraping was cut short: after the bulk pull, one full detail-page fetch, and an attempted batch of ~60 more detail-page requests, the domain (both waqf.zfiusa.org and the zfiusa.org root) became unreachable (curl exit 28 timeouts, WebFetch ECONNRESET) and did not recover within this session's retry window (~5 minutes). Most likely the site's own hosting choked under a moderate request burst (it looks like small/hobby-grade infra) rather than deliberate IP blocking, since even the plain homepage and the zfiusa.org root domain stopped responding. As a result, only ONE property was fully detail-scraped with human-readable name/address/area/status/litigation fields; the sampled bulk-index entries have district resolved to a name but no locality/address/area/status (would require a per-record detail-page fetch, impractical at 45,191-record scale without further engineering -- resuming the scrape once the site recovers, with retry/backoff, and resolving subDistrict/village codes via /waqf-subdistricts, would be the way to get more full records). Recommendation for the hackathon: cite this source cautiously as 'ZFI USA mirror of WAMSI Telangana Waqf data (45,191 properties, snapshot ~Oct 2024)'; use the verified aggregate count and district breakdown confidently; for additional per-property detail, either retry the proven detail-page scrape once the site is back up, or go directly to the presumed primary source, WAMSI (wamsi.nic.in), for a more authoritative/current copy.
